title: introduce regional SLO enforcer with graceful throttle switch and safety rollback
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: after a multi-region incident last month we observed two failure modes: (1) sudden traffic bursts in a single region exhausted GPU pools and tripped coarse circuit breakers, and (2) clients experienced opaque 5xxs instead of predictable degraded behavior. This PR implements a regional SLO enforcer component that performs per-region, rate-aware graceful degradation via a 'throttle switch' and an emergency rollback path. Design in brief: 1) SLO enforcer runs as a daemon on regional control planes and subscribes to the existing metrics stream (latency P50/P95, GPU queue length, model-inflight tokens). 2) When configured SLOs (from console or config map) are violated for a sliding window, the enforcer flips a region-level throttle switch into 'soft-throttle' which instructs edge proxies to reject low-priority requests, switch to a smaller model variant, or add a 30ms synthetic backoff to incoming requests to smooth bursts. 3) If conditions worsen, the switch escalates to 'hard-shed' which triggers cross-region failover per policy. 4) A controller tracks provenance and exposes a safety kill-switch that operators can use to immediately disable automated shedding. This change includes a conservative default policy, a canary rollout plan, observability (metrics + console view), and an ops runbook. Checklist: [x] implement core enforcer and RPC interfaces; [x] hook enforcer to metrics stream; [x] add edge proxy soft-throttle support (graceful reject codes + reason header); [x] console view for region state and recent triggers; [x] automated integration tests for escalation and rollback; [x] add runbook and guidance for support teams. Testing: unit tests for the state machine, integration test harness that simulates token pressure and verifies the sequence soft-throttle -> hard-shed -> failover, e2e smoke in staging with real models. Rollout plan: feature gated off by default, enable for md-1 canary region for 24h, monitor SLO delta and error budget burn, gradually roll to other regions with 6h pause windows. Related: ENG-4521 (regional failover policy), SUP-1243 (customer incident triage). Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the default policy conservative to avoid accidental global shedding; operators must enable aggressive policies via console or config map.

release_notes: Adds a regional SLO Enforcer that supports two-stage graceful degradation (soft-throttle then hard-shed), a console view for region state and an operator kill-switch. Off by default; operators must enable. Improves reliability and traceability during regional overloads.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental aggressive shedding if misconfigured. Mitigation: default policy is conservative, requires explicit enablement; kill-switch and immediate rollback path; canary rollout and metric alarms configured.
testing_instructions: Run make test-unit && make test-integration-ci with the slo_enforcer_simulation fixture. Deploy to staging with FEATURE_FLAG_SLO_ENFORCER=true for md-1, then run the workload generator scripts/ci/integration/pressure_sim.sh and validate the region state transitions in the console and /region/state API.
notes_for_ops: When enabling, set a low-priority selector for background jobs and client SDK traffic that can be shed first. Use the console quick-toggle to pause automated shedding if you observe unintended customer impact. If emergency rollback is needed, run `redwoodctl region disable-auto-shed <region>`; the command is documented in docs/ops/slo-failover.md.
observability_updates: New metrics: redwood_region_slo_enforcer_state{region,policy_version}, redwood_region_throttle_count_total, redwood_region_backoff_seconds_bucket. Added dashboards to console under
